title: Congruence & similarity
examples: When do two triangles have to be congruent?
How do I use the scale factor to find the side lengths?

explain.say: Today we learn about when shapes are exactly the same size and shape. We will look at triangle congruence rules. These rules help us prove triangles match perfectly.

draw.text: Congruence Rules: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS

explain.say: The Side-Side-Side rule says if three sides match, the triangles are congruent. Consider a triangle with sides three units, four units, and five units. Another triangle with sides three, four, and five units must also be congruent.

draw.text: SSS: Sides match, triangles are congruent.

explain.say: The Side-Angle-Side rule requires two sides and the angle between them to match. Look at a triangle with sides five and six, and the angle between them is forty degrees. Another triangle with sides five and six and forty degrees between them is congruent.

draw.text: SAS: Two sides and included angle match.

explain.say: The Angle-Side-Angle rule needs two angles and the side between them to match. Imagine an angle of sixty degrees, a side of ten units, and another angle of eighty degrees. A second triangle with those same measurements is congruent.

draw.text: ASA: Angle, side, and next angle match.

explain.say: The Right-angle-Hypotenuse-Side rule works for right-angled triangles only. If the hypotenuse and one other side match, the triangles are congruent. This is a special case for right triangles.

draw.text: RHS: Right angle, hypotenuse, one side.

faq.q: What does it mean for two triangles to be congruent?
faq.a: It means that the triangles are exactly the same size and shape. Every corresponding side and angle must have the same measure.
asks: What does congruence mean in geometry?

faq.q: When can I use the scale factor?
faq.a: You use a scale factor when two shapes are similar, not necessarily congruent. It tells you how much larger or smaller one shape is compared to the other.
asks: How do I find the scale factor?
What is the scale factor for similar shapes?

faq.q: Do I need all three sides to use SSS?
faq.a: Yes, for SSS congruence, you must know the lengths of all three corresponding sides. If you are missing one, you cannot use this rule.
asks: Can I use SSS with only two sides?
Is knowing three sides enough to prove congruence?

faq.q: If two triangles are similar, are they always congruent?
faq.a: No, they are not always congruent. Similar means the angles match and sides are proportional. Congruent means the sides are exactly the same length.
asks: Is similarity the same as congruence?

faq.q: What is the difference between SAS and ASA?
faq.a: In SAS, the known angle must be trapped between the two known sides. In ASA, the known side must be trapped between the two known angles.
asks: Which rule needs the angle in the middle?
SAS versus ASA, what is the difference?

facts: Congruent shapes have the same size and the same shape.
The scale factor relates corresponding sides of similar shapes.
If two triangles are congruent, their corresponding angles are equal.
RHS is a special case used only for right-angled triangles.

quiz.say: Triangle A has sides 5 cm, 8 cm, and 10 cm. Triangle B has sides 10 cm, 5 cm, and 8 cm. Which rule proves they are congruent?
quiz.why: The SSS rule states that if all three corresponding sides match, the triangles must be congruent.

wrong.0: This rule requires knowing the angle between two sides, which is not given here.
wrong.1: This rule requires knowing two angles and one side, not just the side lengths.
wrong.2: The RHS rule only applies if the triangle is known to be a right-angled triangle.

quiz.say: If a small triangle has sides of 3 and 4, and the large similar triangle has sides of 6 and 8, what is the scale factor?
quiz.why: The scale factor is found by dividing the corresponding side of the larger shape by the smaller shape, which is six divided by three.

wrong.0: This would be the scale factor if the large triangle was smaller than the small one.
wrong.2: This might come from dividing the shorter side by the longer side, which is incorrect.
wrong.3: This is the sum of the two sides, not the ratio between them.

quiz.say: Two right triangles have hypotenuses of 13 units and one side of 5 units. What is the minimum information needed to prove congruence?
quiz.why: Since both triangles are right-angled, knowing the hypotenuse and one other side is enough to prove congruence using the RHS rule.

wrong.0: This rule requires knowing two angles, not just the side lengths.
wrong.1: This rule requires knowing the angle between the two known sides.
wrong.3: You would need the third side length to use the SSS rule.
